# Exact heralded recovery has a quadratic native-query barrier

30 October 2026. Root construction. Independent whole challenge is pending
until its actual receipt is present. This strengthens the coverage lemma in
EXACT_HERALDING_COVERAGE.md. It is an exact-success theorem; approximate
decoding, including the positive adaptive cell, remains outside its conclusion.

## 1. Statement, access and consequence

Use the flat source N_U(X)=U(X tensor I_r/r)U*, logical k>=2, r>=2,
U:C^k tensor C^r -> C^D isometric, D>=kr. All calls are ordinary forward
physical source calls; inputs can be adaptive and entangled with the payload
and retained memory. No source environment, inverse, coherently chosen junk
input, unknown controlled dilation, or U-dependent free advice is supplied.
Every source call used to acquire advice is counted, including offline ones.

An exact success on one already encoded arbitrary payload means the complete
unnormalized logical success subchannel is p_U id, with p_U independent of
the payload/reference. Failure can retain arbitrary quantum history.

For any capped Q-call controller, uniformly in U,

    p_U <= b_r(Q) := Pr[Binomial(Q,1/r)>=r].                (S1)

In particular p_U=0 if Q<r, and

    p_U <= binomial(Q,r)/r^r <= (e Q/r^2)^r.               (S2)

Thus p_U>=alpha>0 requires Q>=r^2 alpha^(1/r)/e. This is an
Omega(r^2) necessary bill for fixed nonzero EXACT success. An exact
repeat-until-success inverse halting almost surely satisfies

    E Q_stop >= r^2.                                      (S3)

These bounds need not be tight: no protocol attaining them is constructed.
For example the exterior-hole decoder's2r-1 queries and small success
probability are consistent with(S1); this theorem does not establish its
minimum-query optimality. Nor is(S2) a lower bound for fixed-error approximate
recovery, and it is NOT a new quadratic theorem for all approximate physical
queries. It does exclude exact success-or-draw as a subquadratic-r route,
even if failures preserve an arbitrarily rich paid history.

# Exact heralding requires complete latent-sector coverage

30 October 2026. Root construction following the completed positive feedback
cell. This is a new internal theorem candidate until its separate whole
challenge is consumed. It is an EXACT-output obstruction, not an improved
constant-error approximate-recovery lower bound or a historical-priority claim.

## 1. Model and theorem

Fix k>=2, r>=2 and d=kr. Restrict the native source to the full-dimensional
subfamily

    N_U(X)=U(X tensor I_r/r)U*,      U in U(d).

Write U_j x=U(x tensor |j>) for its r mutually orthogonal k-column blocks.
Neither j nor the environment is supplied to the controller. Allow arbitrary
definite-order adaptive/entangled FORWARD calls, known controls, instruments,
ancillas and storage. The single payload is already N_U(rho), with arbitrary
reference. Count ALL native calls used for programme acquisition and during
decoding; the original payload preparation is separate. Initially supplied
U-dependent advice, controlled unknown dilations and inverse calls are absent.

A heralded success is exact when its *unnormalized* logical subchannel is

    S_U(N_U(X))=p_U X                         for every X.       (H1)

The scalar p_U can depend on U. Requiring exact normalized success for every
state/reference already forces a state-independent scalar: a completely
positive map whose Choi output is supported on the identity Bell ray has
exactly the form(H1). A failure output may retain arbitrary history. There
is no assumption that the failure is restoring or that the payload precedes
every queried channel.

For an algorithm using at most Q native calls, let

    c_r(Q)=r! S(Q,r)/r^Q

be the probability that Q independent uniform draws cover all r labels.
The convention is c_r(Q)=0 for Q<r.

**Claim. Every such exact success satisfies p_U<=c_r(Q), for EVERY U.**
In particular no nonzero exact heralded inverse exists with Q<r. For any
fixed alpha in(0,1), a uniformly alpha-successful exact inverse requires
Q=Omega(r log r), more explicitly

    Q >= log[alpha*r/(1-alpha)] / [-log(1-1/r)]              (H2)

when the numerator is positive. For alpha=1/2 this gives
Q>=(r-1)log r. An exact repeat-until-success algorithm that halts almost
surely has expected query count at least r H_r. The sharper possible
2r-1 threshold suggested by the exterior construction is NOT proved here.

definite-order physical-query scopes stated in root's
`EXACT_HERALDING_COVERAGE.md` and `EXACT_HERALDING_SCHUR.md`. I sought a
failure in branch collinearity, holomorphic dependence, gauge covariance,
adaptive environment marginals and variable stopping. No substantive
mathematical obstruction was found. This acceptance does not include a
quantitative approximate-error version or a historical-priority assertion.

The separate reviewer-owned `NONFLAT_EXACT_RENEWAL.md` broadens the source
to arbitrary fixed positive junk spectrum; root independently reconstructed
that supplement. The flat proofs are unchanged and do not depend on it.

p_U |Omega_k><Omega_k|. If a positive sum has rank one, each positive
summand has range in that same ray: test a vector orthogonal to the ray
and use that all its nonnegative quadratic forms sum to zero. Thus every
resolved source-label tuple q, known-control environment h and payload
label j has R_qh(U)U_j proportional to I_k. There is no cancellation of
wrong positive branches. The claim remains true at U with p_U=0, where
all those summands are zero.
